title: Milneburg rivalry and what 'runs' means
summary: Allen relays that Punch outplayed Kid Rena and Chris Kelly at Milneburg; Punch explains his 'runs' and clowning in blues playing.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Chris Kelly, the blues trumpeter and his band

blocks.x: I was talking to Sheik about you.
And he was telling me about it in Millenburg. And he said you would run everybody. He said you'd run Rene, Chris Kelly, and all of them.

Yeah, he'd run every Sunday everybody. And then the pavilion. And they were right close together, see. And I was so strong, you know, I was so loud. And the people over on the other pavilion, he was dancing by my music.
He said you could really make those runs. You had it for those runs in those days.
That's what Lewis said today, the round of drums. So, you know, yeah, I had more runs than anybody ever known.
Well, what does that mean? Well, can you give me an example?

Yeah, like, well, take hard society. I played the clown part of that part. And the other trumpet player that do that, see. . See, I played all that kind of stuff, see. And like I'd be playing any kind of blues or something. Well, I put more in it than the other part. Like you said, . I said . All that, that's what's called, you know, run.
. Oh, I got the picture now.
I just want you to explain it, you know, a little more quickly. Yeah, I do.
Stuff in there all the time.
